speaker: The Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) and Second Minister for Defence (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: Disruption can occur, for example, when a participant in a payment and settlement system becomes insolvent.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) and Second Minister for Defence (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: A case in point was in 1995 when the insolvency of Barings transmitted its financial losses to counterparties in the European Monetary Union clearing system.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) and Second Minister for Defence (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: When a participant in a payment and settlement system becomes insolvent, the liquidator of the insolvent participant may try to reverse or “claw back” payments made by that participant, even if the transaction was put through before the participant declared insolvency.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) and Second Minister for Defence (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: This may have a knock-on impact on systemic stability and create significant uncertainty and risk for other participants.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) and Second Minister for Defence (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: Fifteen years ago, MAS enacted the Payment and Settlement Systems (Finality and Netting) Act (FNA) to address this problem.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) and Second Minister for Defence (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: FNA made provision for the protection of payment and settlement systems from disruptions that may generate systemic risks in the financial system.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) and Second Minister for Defence (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: FNA was designed to be technology-neutral, allowing MAS to designate critical payment and settlement systems regardless of technology used.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) and Second Minister for Defence (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: A designated system (DS) consists of (a) participants, which are financial institutions; (b) a settlement institution that maintains the participants’ accounts and settles funds, usually MAS; and (c) an operator to run the system, such as Banking Computer Services Ltd.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) and Second Minister for Defence (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: All these systems are critical to the functioning of Singapore’s financial and payments landscape.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) and Second Minister for Defence (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: Since the enactment of FNA 15 years ago, there has been a proliferation of faster payments systems with different settlement models and longer business hours.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) and Second Minister for Defence (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: The amendments take into account foreign and domestic developments since 2002 in the areas of insolvency protection and regulatory controls for DSs.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) and Second Minister for Defence (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: We have incorporated feedback from a public consultation exercise conducted in August 2017.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) and Second Minister for Defence (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: To clarify, the scope of the FNA and the Bill does not directly cover the regulation of customer-facing retail payment or remittance service providers.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) and Second Minister for Defence (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: Such activities are currently regulated under two separate Acts – the Payment Systems (Oversight) Act (PSOA) and the Money-Changing and Remittance Businesses Act respectively.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) and Second Minister for Defence (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: In November 2017, MAS commenced a separate public consultation exercise proposing to streamline the regulation of payment and remittance service providers under a single and new Payment Services Bill.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) and Second Minister for Defence (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: MAS aims to introduce this new Payment Services Bill in Parliament for First Reading in late 2018, after considering feedback from the public consultation.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) and Second Minister for Defence (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: The key components of a transaction are: (a) the transfer order – a payment instruction from a participant, such as a bank; (b) netting – which is the process of calculating net debit or credit amount from the multitude of transfer orders sent and received by the participant; and (c) the settlement – the discharge of payment obligations.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) and Second Minister for Defence (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: Currently, FNA does not protect a DS if it continues to process, net or settle transactions beyond the calendar day on which a participant becomes insolvent.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) and Second Minister for Defence (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: Such transactions may be affected by the application of insolvency law and this poses financial risks to the participants.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) and Second Minister for Defence (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: This will cater to systems which operate in multiple time zones or where an insolvency of a participant occurs close to the end of a day and spans into the next day.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) and Second Minister for Defence (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: For example, if on 2 January, a participant’s foreign parent bank goes into insolvency in a foreign jurisdiction at, say, 10.50 am New York time, that is same day 11.50 pm Singapore time.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) and Second Minister for Defence (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: The operator of the DS may be unaware of the insolvency of its participant’s foreign parent bank since this occurred outside office hours on 2 January, almost during bedtime.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) and Second Minister for Defence (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: In a 24/7 payment system, transactions from the now insolvent participant would continue into 3 January, whereupon transactions from this participant would be settled.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) and Second Minister for Defence (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: Without the amendment, the settled transactions on 3 January could be unravelled by liquidators since it is after the date of insolvency.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) and Second Minister for Defence (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: This amendment will provide finality and added protection to the participants’ transactions.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) and Second Minister for Defence (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: Credit risk arises when a participant pays out funds to customers in real-time but receives funds from its counterparty in interbank settlement on a deferred basis.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) and Second Minister for Defence (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: An example is the Fast and Secure Transfer System (FAST) where customers receive funds immediately while the participants only settle with one another twice a day on weekdays.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) and Second Minister for Defence (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: Such risks are mitigated by having participants provide collateral to the DS so that this collateral can be drawn upon for settlement in the event of any default by a participant.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) and Second Minister for Defence (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: The Bill introduces amendments to extend insolvency protection to DSs which use collateral.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) and Second Minister for Defence (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: The Bill also introduces amendments to provide that an operator, settlement institution, collateral holder of a DS or an officer or employee of such an entity will not incur liability for any act or omission which was done with reasonable care and in good faith in the execution or purported execution of any relevant function, duty or power under FNA.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) and Second Minister for Defence (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: The Bill introduces criteria for designation, to provide greater clarity to the industry and stakeholders.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) and Second Minister for Defence (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: Designation will focus on critical systems, where a disruption in the operations of such a system may transmit further disruption to its participants, or to the wider financial system or affect public confidence in other payment systems.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) and Second Minister for Defence (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: The amendments will also prohibit an operator or a settlement institution of a non-DS from claiming to be an operator or settlement institution of a DS.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) and Second Minister for Defence (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: Holding out to be an operator or settlement institution of a DS could mislead participants to think that there is statutory protection from insolvency law.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) and Second Minister for Defence (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: The Bill introduces amendments that will strengthen MAS’ administrative powers over a participant, operator, settlement institution and collateral holder.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) and Second Minister for Defence (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: These include MAS’ powers to obtain information and issue directions to rectify outstanding issues.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) and Second Minister for Defence (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: The participant, operator, settlement institution and collateral holder of a DS will have an obligation to notify MAS in the event of a potential insolvency.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) and Second Minister for Defence (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: Together with the improved administrative powers conferred on MAS, the Bill will help maintain confidence in DSs and preserve the stability of Singapore’s financial system.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: They are also in line with the recent changes to the Securities and Futures (Amendment) Bill that I spoke on last year.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: These enhancements will ensure that our national systems and cross-border systems are further protected.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: They will enhance and promote systemic stability in the financial system as well as give MAS a more robust oversight.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: This will happen through improved stability of the key systems and a more secured cross-border system.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: For the banks and financial institutions, this means greater confidence and transparency, and greater readiness for collateral-based systems.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: The amendments see several significant changes which will translate into desirable outcomes.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: One of these changes is the penalty clause.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: Holding key officers accountable is really important as, according to CEO Today magazine, leadership shortcomings will often emerge as a principal underlying cause for bank failures.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: Next, with some more precise designation criteria, the industry and stakeholders will benefit from greater clarity.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: It will also prevent non-DSs from making illicit claims of being a DS, which some are doing to benefit their business, but with the consequence of misleading and disrupting systemic stability.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: This has become considerably more important, in light of another policy change concerning DSs.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: Currently, DS does not have any protection under the 2002 FNA should they continue to process, net or settle transactions beyond the calendar day on which a participant becomes insolvent.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: This creates undue financial risks to the participants.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: Considering that more transactions are occurring globally on a daily basis for both commercial entities and individuals, and the nature of businesses that operate across multiple time zones, this risk is greatly multiplied.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: This will certainly be a welcome move for financial institutions.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: For the DS which utilises collateral as part of their netting and settlement processes, the introduction of collateral security and collateral holder will help extend further insolvency protection and mitigate credit risks.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: Having said that, I would like to raise some concerns regarding these enhancements.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: Can the Minister inform the House where would these changes take place for Singapore compared to other jurisdictions?

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: By this, I mean to ask if any study or consultation has been done on the DS of other countries.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: The rise of fintech has brought about many new technologies and innovations that are vastly different from traditional financial methods in the delivery of financial services.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: How forward-looking are the enhancements in ensuring that transactions via these new technologies are adequately protected?

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: These days, block chain technologies, cryptocurrencies and quick response (QR)-based solutions are growing in popularity.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: If these technologies are also covered under the amendments, then how does this reconcile with the prevention of illicit claims to be a DS?

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: Next, I also note that under the proposed amendments, MAS is to be exempted from certain sections of FNA.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: Can the Minister elaborate further on this self-exemption?

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: In what aspects of the insolvency law are carved out by virtue of FNA?

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: The security of domestic operators of DS is another matter or aspect to consider.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: Banking Computer Services Pte Ltd (BCS) handles the SGD Cheque Clearing System, USD Cheque Clearing System and the Interbank GIRO.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: And the settlement institution for the USD Cheque Clearing System is Citibank NA (Citi), a foreign bank.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: The Bill, when passed, will provide greater security and mitigate risks for the designated payment and settlement systems through systemic and prudential means, which would be a welcome move for financial institutions in Singapore.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Given the rapid development in fintech, we need to ensure our laws and regulations keep up.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: I have comments and queries on one specific aspect of the Bill and, more broadly, to request for an illustration.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: I refer to the Consultation Paper MAS shared dated 3 August 2017 which listed the objectives of the amendments in this Bill.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: The objectives are to bring Singapore’s laws on this subject matter up to date with international developments to enhance Singapore’s position as a major financial centre and to incorporate global best practices from leading jurisdictions, like the United Kingdom (UK) and the European Union (EU).

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: As such, to try and understand the Bill, I have looked into the EU Settlement Finality Directive 98/26/EC, which has been since amended by two other directives in 2009 and 2010 and two regulations in 2012 and 2014.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: In this Bill, I note that clause 9, which amends section 8 of FNA does not prescribe the same degree of certainty as to whether a transfer order or any other transactions in the section 8(1) list will be legally enforceable and binding on third parties as long as a transfer order or any other list of matters is entered before an opening of an insolvency proceeding.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Can the Minister clarify why this is so?

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Prescription of this timing is important to my mind, as cross-border payment settlement and netting seem especially vulnerable to insolvency laws in different jurisdictions.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: I understand that this insolvency carve-out is dealt with in clause 9 of the Bill, which amends section 8 of FNA.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Section 8 of FNA states that transfer orders and the transactions in section 8(1) list "shall not be regarded as to any extent invalid on the ground of inconsistency with the law for distribution of the assets of a person on bankruptcy or winding up, or on the appointment of a receiver, receiver and manager or equivalent officer".

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: I appreciate that this has the implied effect of ensuring transactions made through DSs are final, irrevocable and cannot be reversed or challenged by insolvency laws or a liquidator.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Can the Minister clarify if it is the intention of the Ministry to not draw a distinction and provide a blanket prioritisation and finality of transfer orders and transactions in section 8(1) of FNA?

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: If so, can the Minister further clarify if this may be open to abuse in any way, such as by a company disposing of its assets even after commencement of winding up, contravening section 259 of the Companies Act by effecting transfer orders into a DS?

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Additionally, can the Minister provide specific examples for Members and the public to understand the practical implications of these amendments, specifically the extension of insolvency protection for transfer orders, netting and settlement in a DS amendment?

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: For example, what transactions would not have previously fallen under FNA which will now fall under the revised FNA once the Bill is passed?

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: I appreciate that this is a highly technical Bill, but it is precisely such Bills that require illustrations and explanations.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Alternatively, will MAS be publishing guidelines to help the affected parties, such as the DS operators, settlement institutions, financial institutions and the public, better understand the revised FNA?

speaker: Mr Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: Mr Saktiandi Supaat asked if any study or consultation had been done on the DSs of other countries.

speaker: Mr Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: MAS studied a variety of jurisdictions, such as Australia, Canada, Europe, Hong Kong, New Zealand and the UK, to distil the best practices.

speaker: Mr Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: The proposed amendments are also in line with international standards, such as the Principles for Financial Market Infrastructures, set by the Committee on Payment and Market Infrastructures of the Bank for International Settlements and the International Organisation of Securities Commissions.

speaker: Mr Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: In addition, MAS consulted financial institutions extensively and drew on our experience administrating the FNA over the last 15 years.

speaker: Mr Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: With this Bill, MAS will be among other leading jurisdictions in the area of insolvency protection for DSs.

speaker: Mr Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: Mr Louis Ng enquired about the differences in the timing of insolvency protection between the EU Settlement Finality Directive and the proposed Bill.

speaker: Mr Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: He also sought clarification on the potential abuse of the extended insolvency protection.

speaker: Mr Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: The EU's regime takes a different approach from this Bill.

speaker: Mr Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: There are three insolvency scenarios envisaged by MAS that will require this.

speaker: Mr Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: I have briefly mentioned one of them in my Second Reading speech but will elaborate.

speaker: Mr Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: Second, a system that originates transfer orders on the day of insolvency but settles the next business day.

speaker: Mr Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: For example, FAST transactions which occur on late Friday evening which will be settled between the banks only the next Monday morning, these transactions would now be protected.

speaker: Mr Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: And, as I mentioned in my earlier speech, if a foreign bank branch in Singapore has its parent bank go insolvent close to midnight, Singapore time, the operator of the DS may be unaware of the insolvency of its parent since this occurred outside office hours, until the next business day, whereupon transactions from this participant was already settled.

speaker: Mr Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: The Bill will ensure the DS participants’ transactions, including the foreign bank branch’s transactions, are honoured and protected.

speaker: Mr Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: In the EU’s case, the operator would have to prove that they were not aware, nor should have been aware of the insolvency proceedings.

speaker: Mr Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: MAS has assessed that the challenges in proving this will create significant uncertainty which will defeat the very purpose of giving operators and participants certainty of finality of transactions and then protect the system as a whole.

speaker: Mr Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: Hence, we decided not to subject the operator to such a burden of proof but, instead, provide for a short window where there is certainty.

speaker: Mr Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: Mr Saktiandi Supaat asked a pertinent question about the adaptability of the Bill to future technologies, especially given the robust developments in the payments space.

speaker: Mr Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: FNA is technology-neutral and allows MAS to designate systems which meet the fundamental criteria for designation, where a disruption in the operations of such a system may transmit further disruption to its participants, or to the wider financial system or affect public confidence in other payment systems.

speaker: Mr Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: Hence, as long as the designation criteria are met, whether a system is based on block chain, QR code or biometrics or something we have not seen, MAS will be able to designate the system.

speaker: Mr Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: DSs will be gazetted and publicly listed on MAS’ website.

speaker: Mr Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: This allows any consumer or business to cross-check the system’s legitimacy of being a DS.

speaker: Mr Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: Mr Saktiandi Supaat asked about the exemptions for MAS from certain provisions of FNA.

speaker: Mr Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: This is because MAS operates MEPS+, our nation’s large value SGD real-time gross settlement system and a DS under FNA.

speaker: Mr Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: The amendments provide for MAS to be exempted from the provisions which are administrative in nature, and MAS is exempted from these provisions as MAS cannot be invoking such powers upon itself.

speaker: Mr Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: However, the proposed exemptions for MAS do not affect the insolvency protections provided by FNA for DSs operated by MAS.

speaker: Mr Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: Mr Saktiandi Supaat asked about the contingency plans for commercial entities that operate DSs in Singapore, such as BCS and Citi.

speaker: Mr Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: As a recap, BCS is the DS operator for SGD and USD cheques and Interbank GIRO, while Citi is the DS settlement institution for USD cheques.

speaker: Mr Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: MAS recognises the important role that these operators play in the stability of the financial system.

speaker: Mr Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: The regulation and supervision of payment systems fall under a separate Act, the PSOA.

speaker: Mr Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: BCS and Citi are regulated under PSOA and, thus, closely supervised by MAS.

speaker: Mr Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: Both entities are required to have strong risk management controls in place to address key risks, such as credit, liquidity and operational risks.

speaker: Mr Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: They also need to have business continuity plans and these are validated through industry-wide exercises.
